Paraweapon Deployment Guide
Entry 213: “Antimatter Parasites”
30-Word How-To
Switch container to “immature” and add to enemy water or food supplies, or use “mature” and throw like a grenade. If you or a colleague are contaminated, don’t hesitate — amputate.
Overview:
Asset 213 is a hand-portable steel canister containing a brood of dormant xenoparasites. The Asset may be deployed in two configurations. In
immature
configuration, xenoparasites may be covertly inserted into enemy supplies as a form of biological agent. In
mature
configuration, however, the canister uses UV (ultraviolet) light to induce cannibalism in the brood, leaving one surviving adult xenoparasite. A thrown canister then opens on a timer, releasing the grown parasite to engage enemy forces.
The xenoparasites naturally inhabit a living host, typically entering through the digestive tract, though any physical contact with instances can allow for infestation. The
immature
configuration focuses on infesting enemy personnel. Typically, xenoparasites reproduce when the host experiences intense emotion, disintegrating nearby matter in energetic flashes to fuel themselves. However, due to Foundation conditioning, reproduction is impossible. Instead, heightened emotion triggers autolysis, annihilating the host, their surroundings, and the xenoparasites.
The
mature
configuration centres on a full-grown xenoparasite, which can use its disintegration ability directly, and is secure against essentially all material assault. However, once released, its internal nutrient reserves will suffice for only thirty seconds before it self-terminates. The resulting rampage as it unsuccessfully attempts to sustain itself is the primary offensive effect.
